title: stream-aware trace slate: lightweight streaming-span hook with KV-cache alignment
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem summary:
Existing SDK tracing loses fidelity for streamed LLM responses and across async boundaries: chunk-level timings are not captured, KV-cache hit/miss transitions are not visible in traces, and high-tail latencies during cold-KV or model-fallback events are hard to correlate to downstream errors. This makes debugging user-visible latency spikes and partial-response errors slow and error-prone.

Proposal:
Introduce a lightweight "trace slate" hook in the platform SDKs and middleware which: 1) emits compact chunk-level events (as minimal child spans) for streaming responses, 2) attaches a small, immutable KV-cache alignment token and prompt-prefix fingerprint to the request/span envelope, and 3) exposes opportunistic sampling hints for low-overhead collection of problematic traces (errors, >99p latency, KV miss). The slate is intentionally compact (<=128 bytes payload when encoded) to keep propagation cheap over HTTP/gRPC and across worker queues.

Goals and constraints:
- Low overhead: median CPU overhead <=0.5ms on Node SDK hot path, p50 additional network bytes <200B for header payload when un-sampled.
- Async-safe: works across promises, Node worker threads, Python asyncio, and Go contexts.
- Backwards compatible: new header X-RW-TRACE-SLATE v1 encoded as base64 JSON; older agents ignore unknown header.
- Privacy-compliant: payload contains no user prompts in raw form — only deterministic fingerprints/hashes and kvcache version tags.

Design highlights:
- Envelope span: created at request start, contains attributes: request_id, model_variant, kvcache_version, prompt_prefix_fingerprint, slate_version.
- Chunk spans: created per emitted chunk/stream-frame with tags: chunk_index, token_count, local_elapsed_ms, kvcache_state (warm|partial|cold). Chunks are soft-linked to envelope via lightweight IDs to avoid heavy parent/child allocations when sampling is off.
- Opportunistic sampler: SDK collects full spans only when error or latency threshold breached. Otherwise the envelope plus compact chunk counters are emitted.
- Correlation token: deterministic 48-bit token (RFC-safe) included in header to reconcile spans with console logs/metrics and enable downstream join without full trace.

Implementation plan:
1) Node SDK (initial): middleware + streaming adapter + context propagation hooks (2-week sprint).
2) Server runtime receiver: accept X-RW-TRACE-SLATE header, correlate to internal span id, and attach kvcache metrics to request trace.
3) Console: add a "Stream latency by kvcache state" heatmap and stream-chunk timeline in the trace view.
4) Rollout: start with canary (10% traffic) on dedicated clusters, monitor overhead and error correlation, then ramp.

Compatibility/interop notes:
- Header name: X-RW-TRACE-SLATE; uses base64(json) to enable future fields without wire-breaking.
- Fall back to existing trace propagation headers (traceparent) for full-sampled traces. Slate never replaces OTLP but augments it for stream cases.

Benchmarks (early local harness):
- Synthetic LLM streaming (gpt-like model) workload: median overhead 0.32ms on Node 20, p99 +2.9ms.
- Header payload size (unsampled): 164 bytes.
- End-to-end added bytes for gRPC: +0.1% at 512 token response size.

Observability and dashboard changes:
- New metrics to emit: kvcache.stream_hit_rate, stream.chunk_count_distribution, trace.slate_sample_fraction, stream.kvcache_miss_latency_p90.
- Console additions: stream timeline (chunk-level visualization), heatmap for tail latency vs kvcache_state, and a prebuilt query: "requests where trace.slate.kvcache_state=cold and request.latency>1000ms".

Risks and mitigations:
- Increased traffic for telemetry: mitigated by opportunistic sampling and header compactness.
- Language SDK divergence: implement spec in a small portable reference and tests; start with Node then port.
- Privacy: ensure fingerprints are non-reversible and documented in compliance docs.

Success criteria:
- Can identify and correlate 95% of streaming partial-response incidents to either kvcache cold events or network stalls within the new trace slate traces.
- Overhead validated in canary: median CPU <0.5ms, p99 <10ms additional.

Next steps:
- Land Node SDK PR -> internal QA harness -> server runtime adapter PR -> canary rollout -> console widgets prototype.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Node SDK implements slate header encoding/decoding and emits envelope+chunk counters. 2) Server runtime recognizes header and annotates internal span with kvcache_version and slate token. 3) Canary shows <0.5ms median overhead and no customer-visible error regressions. 4) Console surfaces stream timeline and heatmap for kvcache state.
implementation_notes:
- Reuse existing async context propagation shim from ENG-78012 where possible.
- Keep chunk-span allocations lazily created only when sampling happens; otherwise increment compact counters.
- Use single ring buffer per request to collect chunk summaries; flush on completion or error.
- Add unit tests for header malformed cases and privacy checks.
